chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When an honourable guest of a people comes to you, so honour him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on honouring guests according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the social imperative of karam (generosity) by linking the honor of the guest to the dignity of their tribe, a key concept in Arab customary law adopted by Islam. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining communal harmony and reflecting the Prophet’s (SAW) character in daily interactions, extending respect beyond mere politeness to a spiritual duty of recognizing worth.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever an honourable one of a people comes over to you, so honour him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘When a noble and honorable person of a people comes to you, you must treat him with honor.’”
